Rashi on Temurah 3b:10:1.hebrew: זו היא שבועת שוא - סיפא דההיא משנה דלעיל, הויא האי דקתני זו היא שבועת שוא וכו':
Rashi on Temurah 3b:10:1.english: This is an oath in vain - [This is] the latter clause of that same mishna mentioned above, which has this [wording]: "This is an oath in vain," etc.

Rashi on Temurah 3b:12:1.hebrew: ורישא לאו למעוטי אכלתי ולא אכלתי - דאכלתי ולא אכלתי ודאי חייב על שגגתה קרבן:
Rashi on Temurah 3b:12:1.english: And the first clause is not to exclude "I ate" or "I did not eat" - For [in the case of] "I ate" and "I did not eat," one is certainly liable to bring an offering for its unintentional transgression.

Rashi on Temurah 3b:13:1.hebrew:
ומאי שנא - דממעט את "אוכל ולא אכל" מקרבן, וקא מרבי "אכלתי ולא אכלתי" מסיפא דחייב קרבן?
ומשני: מסתברא רישא למעוטי "אוכל ולא אכל":
Rashi on Temurah 3b:13:1.english:
And what is different - that it excludes [the case of] "I will eat and I did not eat" from [the obligation of] an offering, while it includes [the case of] "I ate and I did not eat" from the latter clause, which obligates an offering?
And [the Gemara] answers: It is reasonable [that] the first clause [comes] to exclude [the case of] "I will eat and I did not eat."

Rashi on Temurah 3b:13:2.hebrew: דקאי בלהבא - דקתני "שבועה שלא אוכלנה", וממעט שבועה להבא, כגון "אוכל" ולא אכל:
Rashi on Temurah 3b:13:2.english: Since it deals with the future - For [the mishna] teaches, "An oath that I will not eat it," and it excludes [an oath pertaining to] the future, such as [saying], "I will eat," and he did not eat.

Rashi on Temurah 3b:13:3.hebrew: אבל קאי בלהבא וממעט לשעבר - בתמיה, כגון "אכלתי" ו"לא אכלתי":
Rashi on Temurah 3b:13:3.english: But it deals with the future and excludes the past? - This is stated as a rhetorical question. [The past oath refers to] for example, "I ate" or "I did not eat."

Rashi on Temurah 3b:14:1.hebrew: לא תיתני מימר - מימר בכלל שאר לאוין שאין בהן מעשה:
Rashi on Temurah 3b:14:1.english: Do not teach "one who effects substitution" - Substitution is included among the other prohibitions that involve no action.

Rashi on Temurah 3b:14:2.hebrew: דבדבורו עושה מעשה - שעושה מחולין קדשים:
Rashi on Temurah 3b:14:2.english: Because by his speech he performs an action - For he makes consecrated [items] out of non-sacred [ones].

Rashi on Temurah 3b:15:1.hebrew: אם לא תשמור לעשות וגו' - וכתיב עד ליראה את השם, שיתיירא שלא להוציא את השם לבטלה. וכן מקלל את חבירו בשם מוציאו לבטלה. וכתיב והפלא ה' את מכותך, שיטול מכות, והיינו מלקות:
Rashi on Temurah 3b:15:1.english: If you will not observe to perform, etc. - The verse continues “…to fear the Name” — that one should fear to utter the Name in vain. And likewise, one who curses his fellow using the Name utters it in vain. And it is written: “Then the Lord will make your plagues wondrous,” meaning that he will receive blows, and that is lashes.

Rashi on Temurah 3b:16:1.hebrew: אפילו שבועת אמת - דקא מזהר קרא דאפילו שבועת אמת לא ליעבד בשם שמים, ואי עביד — "והפלא ה' את מכותך" — הרי שיטול מלקות:
Rashi on Temurah 3b:16:1.english: Even a true oath - For the verse is warning that even a true oath should not be made in the name of Heaven, and if one does so — "then the Lord will make your plagues extraordinary" — [it follows] that he should receive lashes.

Rashi on Temurah 3b:16:2.english: It is written explicitly - that it is permitted to do [so, i.e., to take an oath].

Rashi on Temurah 3b:17:1.hebrew: לפייס חבירו - שלא יהא תובעו ממון. אבל מילקא לילקי, הואיל ומביא עצמו לידי שבועה:
Rashi on Temurah 3b:17:1.english: To appease his fellow - So that he [the owner] will not claim money from him. But he should be flogged, since he brings himself to [the point of taking] an oath.

Rashi on Temurah 3b:17:2.hebrew: ובשמו תשבע - דשבועת אמת שריא למעבד:
Rashi on Temurah 3b:17:2.english: And by His name you shall swear - For a truthful oath is permitted to be done.

Rashi on Temurah 3b:18:1.hebrew: לקיים המצוה - כדי שלא יוכל לחזור בו, שנאמר (תהלים קיט, קו) נשבעתי ואקיימה וגו'. ואהכי איצטריך האי קרא, ובשמו תשבע, לאשמועינן דנשבע לקיים את המצוה מותר:
Rashi on Temurah 3b:18:1.english: To fulfill the mitzvah - So that he will not be able to retract, as it is stated: "I have sworn, and have confirmed it" etc. (Psalms 119:106). And for this reason this verse, "and by His name you shall swear," was needed — to teach us that one who swears to fulfill a mitzvah is permitted.

Rashi on Temurah 3b:18:2.hebrew: הכתיב קרא אחרינא ובשמו תשבע - דתרי קראי כתיבי "ובשמו תשבע", חד בואתחנן וחד בוהיה עקב. חד מיבעי ליה לרב, דנשבע לקיים את המצוה, ואידך לשבועת אמת:
Rashi on Temurah 3b:18:2.english: But isn't another verse written: "and by His name you shall swear" - For two verses are written, "and by His name you shall swear": one in [the portion] Va'etchanan and one in [the portion] Vehaya Ekev. One is needed for [the ruling of Rav], that one may swear to fulfill the mitzvah, and the other is for [permitting] a truthful oath.

Rashi on Temurah 3b:19:1.hebrew: אלא למאי אתא - האי קרא דכתיב אם לא תשמור וגו':
Rashi on Temurah 3b:19:1.english: Rather, for what purpose does it come? - This verse, which states: "If you do not observe, etc."

Rashi on Temurah 3b:19:2.hebrew: למקלל את חבירו בשם - דודאי לקי, אע"ג דלא עביד מעשה:
Rashi on Temurah 3b:19:2.english: [It comes] to teach about one who curses his fellow using the Name - For he certainly is flogged, even though he did not perform an action:

Rashi on Temurah 3b:20:1.hebrew: דהיכא דקא עביד תרי איסורי לא תיסגי ליה במלקות - ואף על גב דלקה, אפילו הכי לא נתכפר עדיין במלקות לחודיה:
Rashi on Temurah 3b:20:1.english: For where he commits two prohibitions, lashes are not sufficient for him - Even though he was flogged, nevertheless he has not yet been atoned for by lashes alone.

Rashi on Temurah 3b:2:1.hebrew: נקיות כלל - דאין מלקין אותו בבית דין שלמטה:
Rashi on Temurah 3b:2:1.english: Absolution at all - That the court below does not flog him.

Rashi on Temurah 3b:3:1.hebrew: אשכחן שבועת שוא - דכתיב (שמות כ׳:ז׳) אשר ישא את שמו לשוא, והיינו שבועת שוא, כגון שהוא נשבע לשנות את הידוע לאדם:
Rashi on Temurah 3b:3:1.english: We have found [a source for] a vain oath - For it is written (Exodus 20:7): "who takes His name in vain," and this is a vain oath, for example, one who swears to change what is known to people.

Rashi on Temurah 3b:3:2.english: A false oath - [The Gemara] explains below what the case is:

Rashi on Temurah 3b:3:3.english: From where do we [know this]? - That one is flogged for it.

Rashi on Temurah 3b:4:1.hebrew: מעשה עבד - ובדין הוא דלילקי, שהרי אכל ועשה מעשה:
Rashi on Temurah 3b:4:1.english: He performed an action - And by right he should be flogged, for he ate and performed an action.

Rashi on Temurah 3b:4:2.hebrew: ולא אכל - אינו לוקה, דלאו היינו מעשה:
Rashi on Temurah 3b:4:2.english: And he did not eat - [he is not flogged,] for this is not an action.

Rashi on Temurah 3b:4:3.hebrew: וכי האי גוונא מי לקי - והוא אומר בתמיה:
Rashi on Temurah 3b:4:3.english: And in a case like this, is one flogged? - [It is stated] as a rhetorical question.

Rashi on Temurah 3b:5:1.hebrew: משום דהויא התראת ספק - דאי אתרו ביה: ״הזהר בך שתאכל הככר שנשבעת עליה״, יכול לומר: ״אין לי בית מיחוש בהתראה זו, דאכתי יש לי שהות״, וכן כל היום כולו. ואפי' כי עבר היום, יכול לומר: ״שוכח הייתי, ולא נזכרתי, לא בשבועה ולא בהתראה״, ואינו לוקה:
Rashi on Temurah 3b:5:1.english: Because it is an uncertain forewarning - For if they warned him, "Be careful to eat the loaf that you swore about," he can say, "I have no cause for concern from this warning, for I still have time," and so too the entire day. And even when the day has passed, he can say, "I was forgetting, and I did not remember, neither the oath nor the warning," and he is not flogged.

Rashi on Temurah 3b:6:1.hebrew: תהא באכלתי ולא אכלתי - כלומר, תהא שבועת שקר בנשבע שלא אכל ואכל, או שאכל ולא אכל. דהכא ליכא שום מעשה, דהא לשעבר נשבע:
Rashi on Temurah 3b:6:1.english: Let it be [the case of] "I ate" or "I did not eat" - That is, let it be a false oath in the case of one who swears that he did not eat when he did eat, or that he ate when he did not eat. For here there is no action at all, since he swore about the past.

Rashi on Temurah 3b:7:1.hebrew: ומאי שנא אכלתי ולא אכלתי - כלומר, מאי איריא דקא ממעט אוכל ולא אכל ממלקות טפי מאכלתי ולא אכלתי? הא בתרוייהו ליכא שום מעשה:
Rashi on Temurah 3b:7:1.english: And what is different [about] "I ate" and "I did not eat" - That is to say: Why is it that [the verse] excludes [one who swears] "I will eat," and then did not eat, from lashes, more than [one who swears] "I ate, or I did not eat"? After all, in both of them there is no act at all.

Rashi on Temurah 3b:7:2.hebrew: שבועת שקר דומיא דשבועת שוא - כדמפקא לעיל מלשוא לשוא, שתי פעמים:
Rashi on Temurah 3b:7:2.english: A false oath, similar to a vain oath - As [the Gemara] derived above, from [the words] "in vain" "in vain," [which appear] twice:

Rashi on Temurah 3b:7:3.hebrew: מה שבועת שוא שהיא לשעבר - דכי נשבע על עמוד של אבן שהוא של כסף, היינו לשעבר, דלשעבר קודם שנשבע הויא אבן כמו שהיא עכשיו. ומה שוא לוקה עליה, כדאמרי' לעיל בב"ד שלמטה מלקין ומנקין אותו. אף שקר לשעבר, דהיינו אכלתי ולא אכלתי, לאפוקי אוכל ולא אכל שהוא להבא:
Rashi on Temurah 3b:7:3.english: Just as an oath in vain, which is about the past - For when one swears about a stone pillar that it is made of silver, this is about the past, since in the past, before he swore, it was stone, just as it is now. And [for] a vain [oath] one is flogged, as we said above: the court below flogs him and cleanses him. So too, a false [oath] is about the past, that is, "I ate" and "I did not eat," to exclude "I will eat" and then he did not eat, which is about the future:

Rashi on Temurah 3b:8:1.hebrew: שבועה שלא אוכל ככר זו וכו' - דהא נשבע תלת זימני שלא יאכל אותו ככר:
Rashi on Temurah 3b:8:1.english: "An oath that I will not eat this loaf," etc. - For he swore three times that he would not eat that loaf.

Rashi on Temurah 3b:8:2.hebrew: אינו חייב אלא אחת - כדאמרינן בשבועות, דאין שבועה חלה על שבועה:
Rashi on Temurah 3b:8:2.english: He is liable only for one - As we say in [tractate] Shevuot, that an oath does not take effect upon [another] oath.

Rashi on Temurah 3b:8:3.hebrew: וזו היא שבועת ביטוי - דקאמר קרא: לבטא בשפתים להרע או להיטיב וגו'. וזו היא שבועת ביטוי — שמוציא בשפתיו שלא יאכל אותו ככר, אבל לא גזיל מידי לחבריה. אבל שבועת העדות ושבועת הפקדון, מביא על הזדון כשגגה אשם:
Rashi on Temurah 3b:8:3.english: And this is the oath of an utterance - As the verse says: "to utter with the lips, to do evil or to do good," etc. And this is the oath of an utterance — that he utters with his lips that he will not eat that loaf, but not [an oath that] "I did not rob anything from my fellow." But [with regard to] the oath of testimony and the oath of a deposit, he brings a guilt offering for an intentional violation just as for an unwitting one.

Rashi on Temurah 3b:8:4.english: To exclude what? - That one is not liable to receive lashes for its intentional violation.

Rashi on Temurah 3b:8:5.hebrew: לאו למעוטי אכלתי ולא אכלתי - דאע"ג דהויא שבועת ביטוי, דלא לקי משום דלהרע או להיטיב כתיב, דמשמע להבא, פרט לשעבר, כגון אכלתי ולא אכלתי. ואכתי שבועת שקר היכי דמי:
Rashi on Temurah 3b:8:5.english: Is it not to exclude "I ate" or "I did not eat" - For even though it is an oath of utterance, one is not flogged, because "to do evil or to do good" is written, which implies the future, excluding the past, such as "I ate" or "I did not eat." But then, what would be the case of a false oath?

Rashi on Temurah 3b:9:1.hebrew: לא מייתי קרבן - משום דלהרע או להיטיב גבי קרבן קאי. אבל ממה נפשך, חייב עליה מלקות, דומיא דשבועת שוא:
Rashi on Temurah 3b:9:1.english: He does not bring an offering - Because [the verse] "to do evil or to do good" is stated with regard to the offering. But either way, he is liable to lashes for it, similar to a vain oath.

Rashi on Temurah 3b:9:2.hebrew: דאמר - [ר"י] במס' שבועות (דף כה.) אינו חייב אלא על העתיד לבא:
Rashi on Temurah 3b:9:2.english: Who said - [Rabbi Yishmael] in tractate Shevuot (25a): He is liable only for [an oath concerning] the future.

Tosafot on Temurah 3b:13:1.hebrew: ומאי שנא - פרש"י: מאי שנא דממעט "אוכל ולא אכל" מקרבן, וקמרבי "אכלתי ולא אכלתי" מסיפא דחייב בקרבן. ולא נהירא, דאי אמר למעוטי "אוכל ולא אכל" לא קשיא מידי, אבל אי אמר איפכא אז תיקשה לך. ור"י פירש: ומאי שנא דמפרש לה כרבי עקיבא? לוקמא כר' ישמעאל, ורישא למעוטי "אכלתי ולא אכלתי" מקרבן, וסיפא למעוטי "אוכל ולא אכל" ממלקות. ומשני: קאי בלהבא כו':
Tosafot on Temurah 3b:13:1.english: "And what is different" - Rashi explained: What is different that [the mishna] excludes "I will eat" [and then he did not eat] from [the obligation of] an offering, while it includes "I ate" [and then he did not eat] from the latter clause, which obligates an offering? But this is not clear, for if [the Gemara] had said this in order to exclude "I will eat" [and then he did not eat], it would not be difficult at all; but if it said the opposite, then it would be difficult for you. And Rabbi Yitzchak (Ri) explained: And what is different, that [the Gemara] explains it according to Rabbi Akiva? Let it establish [the mishna] according to Rabbi Yishmael, with the first clause excluding "I ate" [and then I did not eat] from an offering, and the latter clause excluding "I will eat" [and then he did not eat] from lashes. And [the Gemara] answers: It deals with the future, etc.

Tosafot on Temurah 3b:15:1.hebrew: ומקלל חבירו בשם מנלן - שנאמר: "אם לא תשמור לעשות" וגו', "והפלא". ואזהרתיה מהכא: "לא תקלל חרש", אי נמי מהאי קרא גופיה:
Tosafot on Temurah 3b:15:1.english: "And one who curses another using the Name — from where do we derive this?" - As it is stated: "If you will not observe to perform" etc., "then [the Lord] will make wondrous" (Deuteronomy 28:58–59). And its prohibition is from here: "You shall not curse the deaf" (Leviticus 19:14), or alternatively, from this very verse itself.

Tosafot on Temurah 3b:8:1.hebrew: שבועה שלא אוכל ככר זו שבועה שלא אוכלנה ואכלה אינו חייב אלא אחת - ודוקא נקט "שבועה שלא אוכל" תחילה, דאי אמר "שבועה שלא אוכלנה, שבועה שלא אוכל" — חייב שתים; דשלא אוכלנה משמע כולה, וכי הדר אמר "שבועה שלא אוכל" משמע כלל. ובשבועות (דף כז:) מפרש אמאי תנא "שלא אוכלנה" שני פעמים:
Tosafot on Temurah 3b:8:1.english: "I take an oath that I will not eat this loaf; I take an oath that I will not eat it"; and he ate it, he is liable for only one - And the mishna specifically stated "I take an oath that I will not eat" first, for if he had said "I take an oath that I will not eat it; I take an oath that I will not eat," he would be liable for two [violations]. For "I will not eat it" implies the entire [loaf], and when he then says "I take an oath that I will not eat," this implies [eating] in general. And in Shevuot (27b) [the Gemara] explains why the mishna taught "I will not eat it" twice:
